Welcome to the LM51770 Quickstart Design Tool

This stand-alone tool facilitates and assists the power supply engineer with design of a DC/DC buck-boost converter based on the LM51770 current-mode buck-boost controller. As such, the user can expeditiously arrive at an optimized design by virtue of the following:

- Determine filter inductance and input and output filter capacitances
- Select components for soft-start, input UVLO and dither
- Optimize compensation values, slope compensation, and

Peak Current Limit Margin

Margin above the calculated peak inductor current. Margin must be given to allow for load transients and component tolerances.

Value should be higher then 15% to avoid false triggers.

Sense Resistance:
Use this resistor to sense current and set the cycle-by-cycle overcurrent protection. As such, the calculation takes the required current limit setpoint and the inductor ripple current amplitude to calculate RS.

The threshold in BUCK and BOOST modes is 50mV. The variance of the the peak current limit threshold needs toi be considered within the Peak Current Limit Margin. 

The resistances of RCSA and RCSB are equal for balanced common-mode filtering to the CSA and CSB pins.

Selected Sense Resistance:

This resistor to sense current and set the cycle-by-cycle overcurrent protection. 

The cell gets marked orange if the value is greater then the recommended.

Peak Inductor Current Limit:
Maximum current in the inductor usually occurs at VIN(min) or VIN(max). The result corresponds to current limit and is intended as a guide to inductor selection as it relates to saturation current.
The upper limit of the peak current limit is used for calculation but tolerance of the RS and margin needs to be added.

Max Shunt Dissipation:
Maximum power loss in the shunt resistor occurs at VIN(min) or VIN(max). The result is provided at full load current.

Of course, the dissipation is higher in an overcurrent condition, and the shunt should be rated for this condition.

Slope Compensation Resistance:

According to peak current mode control theory, slope compensation is required at a operation with duty cycle greater than 50%.

It gets marked red if Rs/Lf is not within the recommended range, see Datasheet

Output Voltage Ripple:
Enter the desired maximum peak-to-peak output voltage ripple here. This will set the ideal output capacitance value.

Max output ripple will likely occur at VIN(min) in BOOST mode or perhaps at VIN(max) in BUCK mode.

The text in the cell is flagged red if:
-The output voltage ripple is zero.

Output Capacitance:
Enter the output capacitance here based on the minimum calculated result. Make sure that the nominal capacitance is appropriately derated for applied voltage, particularly with ceramics.

The text in the cell is flagged red if:
-The chosen output capacitor is smaller than the minimum ideal capacitance.
